US Considers Delaying Taiwan Arms Sales Amid Diplomatic Schedule

The United States is reportedly considering postponing the announcement of significant arms sales to Taiwan. This potential delay is being weighed until after the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen and the G20 summit. Sources indicate the decision is linked to Chinese President Xi Jinping's upcoming travel to Washington for a summit. Defence firm Anduril has stated that delays in US arms sales to Taiwan are impacting its business.
